prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1417; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports a left-turn collision at a signalized intersection with an oncoming vehicle. Insured states the other driver entered on a green light. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from insured and awaiting third-party photos.

Entry 2: Contacted the third-party claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed she was not represented by counsel. She reports neck and lower back pain following the impact and says she visited an urgent care clinic the same day. Diagnosis listed as lumbar strain. Advised claimant of the claims process and requested medical records and treatment notes.

Entry 3: Received police report. Responding officer recorded both drivers' accounts and noted no citations issued at the scene. Witness statement from a pedestrian indicates the insured began the turn when the signal turned yellow. Liability remains under review pending signal timing data from the city.

Entry 4: Claimant provided urgent care discharge paperwork. Treatment included x-rays, pain medication, and a referral to physical therapy. Claimant reports missed work for several days and is attending therapy twice weekly. Discussed with claimant that she may wish to keep receipts for all out-of-pocket expenses, including mileage to appointments.

Entry 5: Left a follow-up voicemail for claimant requesting physical therapy progress notes and an updated work status note from her employer. Claimant returned call, confirmed symptoms are improving, and agreed to send documentation by email. Reserve set pending medical review. Will reassess liability once signal timing records are received.
